children: Samsung Electro-Mechanics has signed a 360.5 billion won supply contract for packaging substrates used in memory semiconductors. According to ChainCatcher, citing THE ELEC, the company announced the deal on October 19 with a large global company whose name was not disclosed. The contract runs from January 1 to December 31, 2027, and represents 3.2% of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ consolidated revenue last year.

This is the company’s first disclosed long-term supply contract for packaging substrates. Including this deal, Samsung Electro-Mechanics has disclosed seven long-term supply contracts this year, worth a combined approximately 4.3 trillion won. Previous contracts were mainly for components such as silicon capacitors, multilayer ceramic capacitors and inductors. The new deal expands its long-term contracts into packaging solutions, including FC-BGA and BGA substrates.

Last month, the company announced investments of 4.27 trillion won in its FC-BGA facility in Sejong and 2.51 trillion won in packaging substrate production equipment in Vietnam. As part of a government project, it also plans to invest 8 trillion won at its Sejong site and 15 trillion won at its Busan site by 2040. Samsung Electro-Mechanics plans to produce FC-BGA substrates in Busan, Sejong and Vietnam. A company official said growth in AI and high-performance computing is increasing the importance of high-performance packaging substrates, and that the company will strengthen supply cooperation with customers and build a stable supply system.

title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Signs 360.5 Billion Won Packaging Substrate Supply Contract
